newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares slip, immune to good results.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares slip, immune to good results.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped back on Monday in a bearish market apparently immune to good corporate results by some companies.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its all-share index fell 1.32 points to 358.49 points in turnover worth an average 57.60 million pounds ($16.97 million).

Two large transactions worth a total of 10 million pounds made Delta International Bank the most active share of the day. The 576,000 shares changed hands at 17.36 pounds, which was also the closing price -- 0.82 pounds up on Sunday's close.

"One of the public-sector banks was selling to a strategic investor," said broker Rania Afifi of Intercapital. She did not say which bank was selling but Bank of Alexandria is listed as a major shareholder in Delta International.
The Egyptian government has given its banks instructions to disengage from joint-venture banks like Delta as part of the privatisation programme. Many of them have already done so.
In the milling sector, often a barometer of market sentiment, the trend was generally downwards, Afifi said.
"Upper Egypt Flour Mills had very good 10-month figures but it hasn't affected prices at all," she said.
"When the market's on a fall, it doesn't react positively to any good news," she added.

The company said on Friday it made profits of 56 million pounds in the period July 1996 to April 1997, against 38 million in the same period of 1995/6. The shares ended Monday 2.3 pounds down at 79.70 pounds, the CMA said.
Partially privatised General Silos and Storage also released a positive profits forecast but this failed to stop the shares slipping 2.00 to 93.00 pounds.
The board told a meeting of shareholders on Monday it expected pre-tax profits of 70 million pounds this financial year, against 56.32 million in 1995/6.
Cements, another market barometer, closed mixed. "There's no real pressure on the buy side," said Afifi.
The most active cement company, Amriyah Cement, gained 0.95 pounds to close at 84.95. But Egyptian Tora Portland Cement lost 1.75 to finish at 88.25 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 502.62 points from 505.54 on Sunday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also slipped to 261.99 from 262.66 points.
Out of the 89 shares traded, 34 rose, 33 fell and the other 22 ended the day unchanged.
